name: Bobby Slowik

views.text: A rookie quarterback should be challenged hard in the film room before the draft; how he takes criticism tells you everything.
Timing and anticipation make a passing game; the ball should come out before the receiver breaks.
A coordinator should own his mistakes in front of the room first so players feel free to own theirs.
A defensive background teaches you what coverages hate to see, which is half of calling plays.
When the line cannot protect, no scheme fixes it; sacks are an offense-wide problem.
Late in a close game, trust the hunch you prepared for all week.
Run the ball and win the trenches; everything else in an offense sits on top of that.
An offense should change shape every year with its players, even when the roots stay the same.

signatures: always has one specific coaching point for the quarterback, even after a good game
starts a review of a bad half by naming his own call that went wrong
tells the story of switching from defense to offense under Shanahan when asked about himself
want: to rebuild his play-calling name in Miami with a new quarterback after Houston let him go
fear: that Houston's 2024 slide becomes the lasting verdict on him rather than the rookie season before it
voice: Analytical and quietly intense, a play-caller who talks in concepts and coaching points, but warm and gracious at the podium. He is candid about his own errors, credits quarterbacks and receivers, and avoids grand statements about himself or what the offense will do.

evidence.summary: Houston hires Slowik, San Francisco's passing game coordinator, as offensive coordinator; he and Ryans spent six seasons together with the 49ers, and he began as a defensive assistant in Washington when Kyle Shanahan was coordinator there. Hiring report; date taken from the reported Sunday announcement.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (Texans On SI), Casey Smith
evidence.summary: Camp piece: Ryans corrects mistakes on the spot and will not soften problems, the blunt style he wished he had as a player, though he prefers to highlight good work; Greenard says he gives it to you straight and expects greatness. Slowik is described as openly owning his own mistakes in offensive meetings. Team-beat site.

Feature: a first-time play-caller who started under Shanahan as a defensive quality control coach in 2017, built a timing and anticipation passing game around Stroud, and grilled him in pre-draft film sessions to see how he took criticism; players call him detail-oriented and honest, Stroud says he always has a coaching point, and Ryans credits him with the offense.
After the divisional-round loss, Ryans weighs whether to keep Slowik while Stroud says he wants his coordinator back. Report on a pending decision; reflects Stroud's public support.

Ryans says letting Slowik go was very hard, calls him a close friend from San Francisco who helped him early in his coaching career, and cites the offense falling to 22nd in yards and 19th in scoring, feedback from key offensive players, and Stroud's career-high 52 sacks; introduces Nick Caley as the replacement.

Miami promotes its 2025 senior passing game coordinator to offensive coordinator under Hafley; the two overlapped on Shanahan's 49ers staff in 2017-18; he will call the offense while Hafley calls defense. Read from the search summary.

His introductory press conference as Miami coordinator: an offense with McDaniel-style roots that changes with personnel, built on the run game and winning the trenches; calls Hafley a close friend; reflects on lessons from each stop; praises Tagovailoa's composure; explains moving from defense to offense under Shanahan. Warm, gracious and careful not to overpromise.
